title: runtime/scheduler: add H100 scheduler presets (balanced + throughput-first) with tail-latency guardrails
author: Marcus Reed
body:
Summary
Adds two H100-targeted scheduler presets (balanced, throughput-first) and the associated tail-latency guardrails. Presets are selected via profile config (hardware profiles pack) or explicit override, and are designed to be safe-by-default for Hosted/Dedicated pools where request mix includes streaming + tool-calling bursts.

Motivation
Bench runs on the H100 pools show we can unlock meaningfully higher decode throughput by increasing continuous-batching aggressiveness and relaxing fairness, but naive tuning causes p95 regressions and streaming instability under bursty concurrency. This PR introduces named presets with explicit intent and guardrails, so we can ship repeatable configs and canary them with clear expectations (and rollback knobs).

What’s in this PR (high level)
- New scheduler preset abstraction: `balanced` (default candidate for H100) and `throughput_first` (opt-in).
- Guardrails to cap tail-latency impact:
  - Dynamic backpressure when queue depth or time-in-queue crosses thresholds
  - Prefill/decode fairness floor to prevent decode starvation
  - Streaming-specific max batch age (protects chunk cadence)
  - Hard bounds for queue limits and max in-flight tokens
- Metrics + logs for selected preset and the guardrail activations (to support perf canary + oncall triage).
- Defaulting behavior: if GPU SKU is H100 and profile is unset, we keep current behavior (no implicit switch yet); presets are only activated via profile pack / config override.

Config surface
- `scheduler.preset`: `"h100_balanced" | "h100_throughput_first" | "none"`
- Preset expands into concrete knobs (batching window, fairness weights, queue limits).
- `scheduler.guardrails.enabled` defaults to true for both H100 presets. Individual guardrails can be disabled for experiments, but require explicit config.

Before/after perf summary (benchmark-lab runner, H100 SXM, runtime@main-2025-11-26 vs this branch)
Workload matrix slice used here:
- Models: Llama-3.1-70B (fp16), Mixtral-8x7B (int8), Llama-3.1-8B (fp16)
- Seq buckets: (prompt 256/1k/4k) x (gen 128/512)
- Concurrency: 8 / 32 / 64
- Modes: streaming + non-streaming

Key deltas (median across matrix; higher is better unless noted)
- H100 balanced:
  - tokens/sec: +9% to +14%
  - p50 latency: -3% to -6%
  - p95 latency: within ±2% (guardrails keep p95 from drifting under burst)
  - streaming chunk cadence (p95 inter-chunk): +0–3% (within gate)
- H100 throughput-first:
  - tokens/sec: +16% to +24%
  - p50 latency: -6% to -10%
  - p95 latency: +3% to +8% depending on prompt mix (expected; guardrails cap worst-case but do not eliminate tradeoff)
  - streaming chunk cadence (p95 inter-chunk): +4–9% under high concurrency (flagged as “throughput-first” tradeoff; not default)

Notes
- The throughput-first preset is intended for batchy, non-interactive workloads or dedicated pools where customers accept tail-latency tradeoffs for unit economics.
- The balanced preset is the candidate for general H100 pools once the hardware profile pack is ready to roll out behind perf canary gates.

Testing
- Unit tests: preset expansion + guardrail bounds
- Integration: scheduler config round-trip and preset selection
- Perf: benchmark-lab matrix runs attached in CI artifacts; canary links in comments

Rollout plan
1) Land code behind preset selection only (this PR).
2) Enable `h100_balanced` via profile pack in 1 canary pool (us-east) with perf-canary gating (p95, retry rate, inter-chunk).
3) Gradual region expansion; keep `throughput_first` opt-in only.
4) Rollback: set `scheduler.preset=none` at pool config level; guardrail toggles remain available for quick mitigation.

Risk
Medium. Changes are isolated to preset selection and guardrail plumbing, but they touch the hot path of request admission and batch formation. Guardrails are conservative and bounded; presets are not enabled by default in this PR.

Release notes (internal)
- Runtime: Adds H100 scheduler presets (balanced + throughput-first) with tail-latency guardrails; presets are selectable via config/profile pack. No default behavior change unless preset is enabled.
commits: scheduler: introduce preset registry and expansion into concrete knobs
scheduler: add guardrail hooks (queue age, queue depth, streaming max batch age)
metrics: emit scheduler_preset_selected + guardrail activation counters
tests: add preset expansion unit tests and bounds validation
docs(comment): update config reference strings and examples
conversation: Sofia Ivanova (review): The preset split makes sense. Two requests: (1) ensure fairness floor cannot be set to 0 via preset; (2) please document how streaming max-batch-age interacts with chunk cadence gates. Also, can we rename `throughput_first` to make it explicit it’s not safe for interactive? Maybe `throughput_first_noninteractive`?

Marcus Reed (author): Added validation that fairness_floor >= 0.15 for both H100 presets, and config validation rejects < 0.10 unless `scheduler.guardrails.allow_unsafe=true` (internal-only, not exposed via profile pack). Added comments in preset YAML about streaming max-batch-age. Re naming: I’d like to keep the key short since it’s already referenced in ENG-4824 drafts; I added an explicit warning in config docs + startup log: “throughput_first may increase p95 + inter-chunk latency; not recommended for interactive.”

Neha Kapoor (review): Please add an explicit rollback knob that oncall can flip at pool-level without redeploy. Also want a counter for “guardrail triggered due to queue age” and a log line with thresholds at startup.
Marcus Reed (author): Rollback is `scheduler.preset=none` (pool config). Added `scheduler_guardrail_queue_age_trips_total` and startup log now prints guardrail thresholds when preset != none.

Rina Kobayashi (review): Perf numbers look good, but can you include a breakdown by streaming vs non-streaming and call out worst-case p95 deltas? Perf-canary gates will need a bound that matches reality.

Marcus Reed (author): Updated body with streaming cadence deltas and added comment linking to the matrix artifact. Worst-case p95 for throughput-first is +8% in 4k->512 under concurrency 64; balanced worst-case +2.1% (one cell).
Lena Fischer (review): One more nit: queue limit defaults—can we make them proportional to `max_concurrency` rather than absolute? Absolute values break on small dedicated pools.
Marcus Reed (author): Done. Queue limits now scale by `scheduler.pool_target_concurrency` with min/max clamps. Added integration test for small pool config.
Noah Patel (review): Please ensure no behavior change when preset is unset. Also, do we expose which preset is active in debug dumps?
Marcus Reed (author): Confirmed default path stays the same unless preset is explicitly set. Added `scheduler_preset_selected` to effective-config dump and startup logs.
Sofia Ivanova (approval): Approved. Please make sure ENG-4824 references this PR and that the profile pack uses balanced as the default candidate. Also thanks for keeping guardrails on by default.
Neha Kapoor (approval): Approved from SRE side given preset is opt-in and metrics/rollback are present.
release_notes: Runtime (scheduler): Add H100 scheduler presets `h100_balanced` and `h100_throughput_first` with tail-latency guardrails and observability. No default behavior change unless presets are enabled via config/profile.
